title: Anchorscape: Mini-dashboard anchors and contextual navigation for Console
creator: Lena Thompson
description:
Problem: Engineers and product users land on the Redwood Console and must click through multiple layers to reach high-value surfaces: dashboards (cost, latency), rollout controls, and per-workspace views. Current left-rail and workspace switch patterns cause context loss and duplicate navigation paths across routes.

Goal: Prototype and validate a compact, persistent set of ‘anchors’ (mini-dashboard widgets + entry anchors) in the top-level navigation area that surface cost, rollout status, and workspace picker with minimal context switch cost. The solution should reduce average clicks-to-dashboard by >= 30%, preserve deep-route context when switching workspaces, and scale to add more anchors (alerts, quotas) later.

Scope: Design and test IA patterns, high-fidelity prototypes for desktop and tablet, accessibility pass (keyboard + screen reader), handoff spec for engineering (ARIA roles, route transitions, analytics hooks). Excludes mobile redesign and changes to account-level billing flows in this ticket.
acceptance_criteria: Prototype with three anchors: Cost snapshot, Rollout health, Workspace selector, available in both Workspace and Org contexts
User testing (n=8) shows 30% fewer clicks to reach cost dashboard compared to baseline task flows
Design spec includes route-preservation behavior: when switching workspace, open route attempts to map to equivalent route in target workspace if available; fallback to landing anchor when not
Handoff artifacts: Figma frames + component tokens, interaction spec, and analytics events documented in Confluence
Accessibility: keyboard focus order defined; screen reader labels for each anchor; contrast checks pass WCAG AA
decisions: Adopt anchor strip at the top of main content (below global header) rather than left-rail to preserve vertical space for console pages
Use compact live-snapshot mini-cards (single line metric + sparkline) for Cost and Rollout anchors; clicking expands to full dashboard route
Workspace selector will be a contextual popover anchored to the right of anchors; selecting a workspace attempts deep-route mapping rather than forcing the user back to home
Avoid global persistent left-rail duplication; left-rail will remain for low-frequency admin actions, anchors handle high-frequency surfaces
Telemetry: emit anchor_click and anchor_expand events with previous_route and target_route for rollout analysis
